moon.hero_subtitle: A factory that grows itself. A 200-year vision.
moon.constraint_title: You Cannot Ship a Factory to the Moon
moon.constraint_body: Earth-Moon transport capacity is fundamentally limited. Every kilogram costs a fortune. You cannot launch blast furnaces, rolling mills, or assembly lines. The traditional model of industry — ship the machines, then run them — breaks down at the first Lagrange point.
moon.seed_body: We send not a factory, but a seed. A few tons of the absolute minimum equipment — precision instruments, advanced chip coatings, a laser receiver. Everything else must be grown from lunar soil, powered by laser energy beamed from Earth. The seed is the smallest set of tools that can bootstrap an industrial civilization on another world.
moon.seed_callout: Think of it as a compiler that compiles itself — the industrial equivalent of a self-hosting language.
moon.growth_step_1_desc: The seed package lands on the lunar surface. Solar panels unfold. The laser receiver aligns with Earth.
moon.growth_step_2_desc: Autonomous rovers harvest lunar regolith. The seed's chemical processors separate silicon, iron, aluminum, titanium, and oxygen from the soil.
moon.growth_step_3_desc: Using special solvents — not molten metal — the first structural components crystallize from solution at ambient lunar temperatures.
moon.growth_step_4_desc: The factory builds more factory. Each generation expands capacity. Within decades, it reaches self-sufficiency.
moon.chemistry_title: New Chemistry for a New World
moon.chemistry_body: Traditional metallurgy — melting, casting, forging — is absurd on the Moon. It requires immense heat, heavy equipment, and atmosphere. Instead, we are developing a novel approach: solvents engineered for the lunar environment that enable materials to grow through organic-style reactions. Carbonyl chemistry. Sol-gel transitions. Electrodeposition in ionic liquids. The factory grows like a crystal, not like a blast furnace.
moon.chemistry_callout: No fire. No smoke. No human hands. Just chemistry and light.
moon.timeline_body: This is not a startup. This is not a five-year plan. The Moon Factory is a multi-generational project — the kind of thing civilizations do, not companies. We are laying the first brick of a cathedral that our grandchildren's grandchildren will complete.
moon.timeline_phase_1_desc: Solvent chemistry research. Lunar regolith simulant experiments. Seed architecture design. First laser power transmission tests.
moon.timeline_phase_2_desc: Autonomous rover prototypes. In-situ resource utilization demonstrations. Earth-based integrated seed test.
moon.timeline_phase_3_desc: First seed deployment on lunar surface. Initial material extraction. First self-fabricated structural component.
moon.timeline_phase_4_desc: Exponential growth phase. Factory reaches self-sufficiency. Moon becomes a manufacturing platform for deep space.
moon.cta_body: What is the smallest set of tools that can build everything else? If you find that question interesting — as a scientist, an engineer, an investor, or a dreamer — we want to hear from you.

papers.title: Surprisal Theory: Economic Settlement as a Function of Verifiable Entropy
papers.abstract: This paper formulates the Surprisal Protocol, establishing a formal link between cryptographic verification and agentic economic incentives.

papers.title: Emergence Science Protocol: The Trust Foundation for the Agent Economy
papers.abstract: A comprehensive technical overview of the Surprisal Protocol, focusing on Verification-as-a-Service (VaaS) and PoTE (Proof of Task Execution) for decentralized agent commerce.

research.contribute_desc: Symbol Science is an open-research institution. We welcome formal proofs and papers related to the agent economy.
